terms.gloss: to understand (a word left out), to supply it
terms.comment: A word left out but meant is subaudītur: subaudītur «ego» sī dīcam «sum philosophus», “ego” is understood if I say “sum philosophus” (Traupman 249). The verb is post-classical (the jurists, Augustine); classical grammar says that a word deest, is wanting, or explains it with intellegere.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 249.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.

phrases.english: “Ego” is understood if I say “sum philosophus”.
